title: Turn a loose Asimov humanoid leg over on the table, then seat its knee side plate flush in the pocket
keywords: side plate on nine M3 inserts
turn a heavy part on the table
instruction: Turn the leg onto its back, then seat the knee side plate flush in its pocket with its nine bolt holes over their inserts, and move both hands clear.
context: Robotics technicians assemble humanoids from makers' guides; Menlo's open-source Asimov 1 is built this way, in a market of about 7,000 humanoids sold in 2025 (IFR) or 13,000 shipped (Omdia). Left Leg Step 8: turn the leg so the thigh's bearing faces up, fit side plate 600_08A on housing 600_10C so the protrusion fits the bearing and all holes align with the threaded inserts, then tighten nine M3x10 bolts. A cocked plate puts holes off the inserts. The 3.03 kg leg (twice the arm's 1.5 kg payload) lies loose on its side and is tipped onto its back, not lifted. Three fits meet on one axis within 5 mm: plate in pocket 0.3 mm a side, pad 34.8 in 35.0 mm bore, boss 11.85 in 12.0 mm bearing. The review did not say whether fasteners are driven, so we added nine bolts in a holder and a screwdriver as free props. Scope: turning a non-cylindrical leg over and seating the plate on its locating features; driving screws is a separate, well-covered act, not scored.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of the table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. All parts are from Menlo's Asimov 1 repository (github.com/menloresearch/asimov-1, CERN-OHL-S-2.0): shapes from the maker's STEP files (the thigh from the maker's URDF mesh). Leg, as after the guide's instruction 3, off the body and loose on the table, nothing holding it: the thigh assembly (URDF left_hip_yaw_link: 1.949 kg, with its centre of mass and inertia) slotted into the knee housing 600_10C (MJF PA12, 1,069.5 cm3 at 1.01 g/cm3: 1.080 kg; the URDF's 2.48 kg knee link includes the calf's later parts), 3.03 kg in all and 54 cm long. Its knee joint is free: the housing turns on the thigh about the bearing's axis, from straight to 1.50 rad bent (URDF), against the unpowered knee actuator's published friction, 0.70 N m to start it and 0.02 N m once it moves, with 0.034 kg m2 reflected inertia (Menlo's actuator table, EC-A4315-P2-36, docs.menlo.ai/asimov/1/reference/joint-design-and-actuation). It starts straight, lying on its side along y with the shank toward -y, the housing's outer face (the plate side) upright and facing away from the robot (+x), the pocket's centre at (46, -7), 6.3 cm up. On its back, the task's turned pose, it rests on three points with that face up, about 4 degrees off level, the pocket's centre at about (31, -6), 10.3 cm up: from its side it tips 86 degrees toward the robot over its lower edge, its centre of mass rising from 6.2 to 7.9 cm (over the edge at 38 degrees) and falling to 5.3. In the outer face, the pocket for the plate: 5.0 mm deep, the plate's own outline with 0.3 mm clearance (80.0 mm across its round end, 40.0 mm across its neck, its narrow end toward the shank), with a 35.0 mm bore at its centre and nine M3 threaded inserts. Its walls stand full depth round the round end and the neck's root and fall away along the neck, where the housing's surface curves down. The thigh's flanged bearing 600_11X (12.0 mm bore, 5.0 mm wide) is on the pocket's axis, its face 11 mm below the housing's face. Plate 600_08A: aluminium 7075, a 5.0 mm sheet 149.4 mm long, 79.4 mm across its round end and 39.4 mm across its neck, 1 mm chamfers on its edges; on one face a 34.8 mm pad (5 mm), a 15 mm step (1 mm) and an 11.85 mm boss (5 mm, 0.9 mm tip chamfer); nine 3.2 mm countersunk holes; 120 g (42.6 cm3 at 2.81 g/cm3). It starts boss down in the socket (36 mm across, 12 mm deep) of an acetal kitting post 50 mm across and 30 mm tall at (20, -17), its sheet on the post's rim, its narrow end toward -y. Friction 0.3 (PA12 and aluminium on the table, on acetal and on each other). Fasteners (Step 8, instruction 5), laid out for the next step and not used in this one: nine M3x10 flat bolts, DIN 7991 (3.0 mm thread, head 6.0 mm across, 1.7 mm tall, 2 mm hex socket), stand head up in a printed holder 40 x 40 x 8 mm at (17, 3), and a hex screwdriver (Wiha SoftFinish 356, 2.0 x 60 mm: 164 mm long, 23 mm handle, 60 mm blade, 25 g) lies on the table, its middle at (12, -6), heading 75 degrees from x. Both are free bodies (the bolts and their holder are one body) with colliders at true size, clear of the leg's and the plate's paths and of both arms at their ready pose; the screwdriver is not driven. Nine brass M3 heat-set inserts, 4.4 mm across and 4.5 mm long, sit in the housing's insert bores (STEP), 0.5 mm under the pocket's floor, under the plate's nine holes. Both arms start at their ready pose. The demo grips at 38 N a finger and presses about 10 N. Real-trial protection and a low-cost stand-in (printed, ballasted to 3.03 kg, pin hinge with a friction screw, gauge-pin fits) are in the README.
scoring: Measured at the end with an inclinometer and a ruler on the housing's face, a depth gauge on the plate's top against the face at ten points round its outline (round end, fillets, neck, narrow end), a 2.4 mm pin gauge and a tape. Score 0 if the plate or the leg falls off the table. Rungs are cumulative: 0.25 with the leg on its back on the table (the face within 10 degrees of level, at its resting height within 12 mm: lying there, not held up); 0.5 with that and the plate in the pocket's mouth, its boss's axis within 1.5 mm of the bearing's and no point of its top more than 4.0 mm above the face (the rim, pad and boss each at least 1 mm in); 0.75 with the plate seated flat, every point within 0.5 mm of flush and level with the face (tilt under 1 degree, boss down); 1.0 with that, every bolt hole on its insert, ready for its M3x10 bolt: the pin gauge passes through each of the nine 3.2 mm holes into its insert's thread (axis within 0.45 mm: 0.4 through the hole, 0.05 into the 2.5 mm minor diameter), no gripper within 10 cm of the plate and the face round it or within 8 cm of the leg's centre line (thigh's end, knee, calf's end), and the plate and leg still (plate under 1 mm in 1 s; leg under 2 mm/s and 0.6 deg/s), held for 1 s and still true at the end. A plate set in the pocket before the leg was on its back, pressed home with the leg moved 15 mm, or its face turned 3 degrees, from how it lay when the plate first reached the mouth, or never carried by a gripper (10 steps in a row 1 cm up with a fingertip within 3 cm), scores at most 0.5. Driving the bolts is not scored. No hold is needed during the press: the leg stays put on its own, so no hand should hold it. Real trial: the same gauges, tape marks round the leg, and a photo, with the bolt holder and the screwdriver set aside.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. Plate, pocket, bearing and insert bores are the maker's STEP geometry; no collider widened: rim 0.30 to 0.34 mm a side, pad 0.10 to 0.12, boss 0.075 to 0.09. Friction 0.3. Knee friction (0.70, 0.02 N m) is a coded drive; the arm presses about 10 N. The bolts and the screwdriver are free props with colliders; nothing uses or scores them. Inserts are visual, in their bores. The demo reads the leg's and plate's poses. Real trial: a printed, ballasted leg (setup).
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials, lift the plate out of the pocket with a suction cup on its top (or by its neck's flats) and set it boss down in the kitting post's socket, straighten the knee, and tip the leg back onto its side, plate side away, on its tape marks.
